The correctness review finds one stale instruction in the active specification index.

**Verdict: Request changes.** Correct the instruction before migration acceptance. No additional correctness or scope-creep finding appears in the reviewed live-code changes.

- **[P2] Required — [hard: spec/SPEC-maintainer-workflow.md:11, retirement of competing instructions]**
  File: `spec/README.md:10`.

  Quoted hunk: “The migration is in progress; the original startup owner remains active until the cutover.”

  The specification requires: “Retire the old workflow and its competing instructions.” It also requires “Keep one current owner for each fact” at line 56.

  Task 11 removes that original owner. The current handoff states that the new workflow is active. Every fresh session must read this index, so the stale sentence supplies a conflicting startup instruction at the acceptance boundary.

  **Fix:** Remove the old-owner activation claim. Link to the sole current handoff for activation and task state. Recheck the fresh-session probes after that correction.

Review scope: the fixed diff from `1b5d08a420f7f916b0c87b166527c60985937f4d` to `632a392291a6761ea7f8f2460a7cac05ff2bc4ec`. I read the approved specification and commit list before code, then the new migration tests and changed tests. I reviewed the migration guard, runner, moved driver/fixture comparisons, active entry points and live reference consumers. Standards include AGENTS.md, the four agent guides, and documentation/package guidance.

The runner retains 24 invocations, archive arguments, audit output selection and both scoped modes. The guard tests cover corrupt evidence, incomplete records, unsafe destinations and old active references. Driver comparisons retain assertion and coverage behavior.

Limits: this pass does not repeat the existing semantic-record reviews or raw-evidence integrity proof. It starts no tests, builds, installs or browsers. The parent owns the clean-candidate gate and actual host probes; their completion is not assumed. The three external release-link corrections remain an explicit approval gate.

The final readability review finds one stale instruction in the frozen candidate.

**Verdict: request changes for the known index correction.** No additional required readability or simplicity finding remains.

Fixed comparison:

```text
git diff 1b5d08a420f7f916b0c87b166527c60985937f4d 632a392291a6761ea7f8f2460a7cac05ff2bc4ec
```

**Required — [hard: spec/SPEC-maintainer-workflow.md:56, one current owner for each fact]**

Location:

```text
spec/README.md:10
```

Quoted hunk:

```text
The migration is in progress; the original startup owner remains active until the cutover.
```

The cutover is complete. The shared instructions and status identify the new workflow as active. This mandatory startup document contradicts them. A fresh reader must decide which instruction owns startup.

Fix: remove the stale startup-owner claim. Keep the link to the sole current status. This duplicates the correction already identified by the coordinator.

The remaining reviewed changes improve navigation and naming. Stable check identities replace filename-dependent behavior. The verifier keeps migration policy in one module, with explicit exceptions and descriptive regression cases. Its length reflects the named integrity and reference boundaries; no speculative framework or compatibility layer appears. Workflow guidance now defines the migration terms.

The review covers the shared entry points, ownership and verification guidance, approved specification/plan/tasks, verifier and tests, runner changes, recipe references, and representative moved drivers. Standards are AGENTS.md, both mapped glossaries, docs/agents/{domain,repository,verification,workflow}.md, and docs/development/documentation.md. The approved specification is spec/SPEC-maintainer-workflow.md. The supplied commit list and recorded migration proofs bound mechanical and historical review.

Limits: this axis does not repeat every semantic batch review or run builds, tests, installs, or browsers. The coordinator's full gate and actual host probes remain separate acceptance evidence. The three external release-link corrections remain an explicit approval gate, not forgotten work.

The architecture review finds one required startup-routing correction in the fixed cutover candidate.

**Verdict: Request changes.** The architecture otherwise improves ownership and removes competing workflow layers.

**[P2] Keep activation state in its current owner.** [hard: docs/agents/workflow.md:3–8, one owner per fact; current phase belongs to STATUS]

Location:

```text
spec/README.md:10
```

Quoted added hunk:

```text
The migration is in progress; the original startup owner remains active until the cutover.
```

Every fresh session must read this index. Its assertion conflicts with the activated root instructions and STATUS. The former startup owner is removed. This leaves two competing statements about which workflow controls the session.

Fix: remove the duplicated activation assertion. Keep the existing link to STATUS as the sole current-state owner. Recheck the cold-start scenarios after this correction.

The inspected structure otherwise follows the approved specification:

- Five local skills and their routing layer disappear. Selective context routing replaces mandatory reading of every decision and research record.
- Live acceptance drivers have one scripts owner. Saved evidence has a separate documentation owner. Six drivers still share the existing browser-distribution helper.
- Three filename-based runner policies become explicit check identities. The renamed-path regression preserves all 24 invocations.
- The migration verifier stays outside product modules. Its fixed-scope exceptions and integrity checks do not create another workflow manager.
- Product source, package manifests, versions and dependencies remain unchanged. Consumer documentation retains its shared release projection.

I checked all twelve smell heuristics. No additional actionable architecture smell appears in the inspected live changes.

Review bounds: baseline 1b5d08a420f7f916b0c87b166527c60985937f4d to candidate 632a392291a6761ea7f8f2460a7cac05ff2bc4ec; specification: spec/SPEC-maintainer-workflow.md. Standards include AGENTS.md, docs/agents/{domain,workflow,repository,verification}.md and development documentation/stack guidance. I inspected entrypoints, runner changes, the complete verifier, moved dependency edges and producer consumers. Mechanical integrity and historical conversions use the supplied task proofs. I ran no builds or browsers. The final gate and host sessions remain pending. Three external release-link corrections remain an explicit approval gate.

Security review of the maintainer workflow migration is complete.

**Verdict:** No actionable security finding in the fixed diff.

```text
Baseline:  1b5d08a420f7f916b0c87b166527c60985937f4d
Candidate: 632a392291a6761ea7f8f2460a7cac05ff2bc4ec
```

- Reviewed the approved specification, commit list, repository standards, shared instructions, Claude settings, and changed live entry points.
- Read the new migration verifier. Repository paths reject traversal and escaping symlinks before content reads. Git calls use argument arrays. Parsed Markdown and source remain data; the verifier does not execute their content or fetch their links.
- Compared relocated drivers against their original files. Process launches, cleanup calls, file-serving calls, and listener bindings retain their security behavior. Reviewed changed fixture paths, output paths, archive selection, and extracted fixture inputs.
- Component source, package manifests, the lockfile, and CI workflows have no changes. The npm-cache proof retains its synthetic credentials, local server, isolated temporary cache, and cleanup.
- Scanned all 1,160 added or changed text files at the candidate for seven credential-pattern classes. No matches occurred. The scan skipped 107 binary files.
- Shared instructions retain task-scoped authorization. External publication still requires approval. Retrieved documentation remains reference data.

**Limits:** This is a static review of the fixed diff. Pattern scanning does not prove that every possible secret is absent. Historical record semantics and raw integrity use the separate migration proofs. I did not run builds, installs, browsers, a new dependency-advisory lookup, or host sessions. The parent owns the running full gate and fresh-host checks; this review does not claim they pass.

The existing npm-token rotation remains owner-controlled and unconfirmed. Its issue preserves that limit. The three external release-link corrections remain a documented approval gate, not forgotten work.

The performance review finds no required changes in the fixed migration diff.

Verdict: pass for the performance axis, limited to static review.

- Component source, package source and styles have no changes. Recipe metadata and comparison-tool changes update references only.
- The check runner retains its fixed browser plan. Stable check identities replace filename matching without adding browser invocations.
- The added strict typecheck covers relocated verification code. This is the approved verification scope, not repeated runtime work.
- The migration guard reads baseline blobs through Git batch operations. It caches parsed Markdown documents and limits traversal to repository inputs. Synchronous reads occur in this command-line check, outside application requests and rendering.
- Inspection of all 37 mapped TypeScript modules compares their call and loop structure. Relevant deltas add bounded setup, type support or extracted-fixture reads. They introduce no additional browser-engine loops, repeated builds, fetch loops or polling.

The approved specification, repository standards, commit list and task-8 evidence inform this review. Earlier integrity and semantic reviews support the mechanical and historical scope. Their results do not certify the final candidate.

Limits: no profiling, timing comparison, build, browser session, installation or test run occurs in this review. Static inspection finds no concrete introduced performance defect; it does not establish measured latency or memory bounds. The coordinator owns the running full gate and fresh-host checks. # Pinned Bun audit source investigation

Date: 2026-10-22. Repository candidate: `5f74c3a0ceb57e2c5a54afe7e23bac91b9bbebb2`.

**Finding:** two native requests report HTTP **503** from the bulk advisory endpoint. Later, the original configuration succeeds unchanged. The repository wrapper hides the failed requests' native error with a JSON parse failure. The masking defect is confirmed; the transient request failure's precise cause remains unverified. Credential causation is not established.

## Observed evidence and version boundary

The coordinator reports that static, build, strict types and all 1,118 unit tests pass before audit fails. The first native audit waits about five minutes, exits 1 and produces empty stdout. The direct retry uses the same pinned runtime. Its saved files now contain zero stdout bytes and this 79-byte stderr diagnostic:

```text
error: POST https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk - 503
```

I read those two file sizes and the stderr diagnostic under `.artifacts/task12-native-audit/`. I did not start, stop or change the coordinator's process.

The coordinator also reports that the actual escalated audit environment has no HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY or NO_PROXY variables. Its connection goes directly to `104.16.11.34:443`. The earlier proxy-presence observation came from the default sandbox environment and does not describe the audit process. Escalated pinned-Bun fetch of the public registry ping returns 200 in about 83 ms. A curl bulk-advisory POST with a simple public lodash payload returns 200 and valid JSON. These prove those specific requests work; they do not reproduce the native audit request.

The local executable reports Bun 1.4.2. The official release points to commit `744846f844374847c902b5e7fd59b4342a51ef99`, matching its recorded build identity. All source links below use that release tag. [Release and commit](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.4.2).

## What the pinned implementation does

| Subject | Source-backed result |
|---|---|
| Audit request | Audit selects npm lockfile resolutions, groups packages by configured registry, deduplicates package versions and sends each group's JSON. It compresses the body with gzip level 6 and sends JSON accept/content-type plus gzip content-encoding. Registry token/auth fields become Bearer/Basic authorization. It appends the bulk-advisory route to the selected registry. [Audit source, lines 317–541 and 643–704](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/runtime/cli/audit_command.rs#L317). |
| Native failure output | Requests run sequentially through the synchronous HTTP client. For the default registry, status 400 or greater prints the POST error to stderr and exits 1. That occurs before the normal JSON-output branch. Thus empty stdout with status 1 is a supported failure path. The observed 503 is a status response, not evidence that Bun's timeout fired. [Audit source, lines 544–574 and 705–737](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/runtime/cli/audit_command.rs#L705). |
| Proxy selection | PackageManager delegates to its environment loader. HTTP and HTTPS use their matching lowercase variable first, then uppercase; NO_PROXY supports exact hosts, domain suffixes, ports and `*`. The pinned loader does not have the current documentation's ALL_PROXY fallback. No proxy cause is established for the actual no-proxy audit process. [PackageManager, lines 824–827](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/install/PackageManager.rs#L824), [environment loader, lines 153–171 and 302–414](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/dotenv/env_loader.rs#L302). |
| Synchronous client | `init_sync` uses normal client defaults with the selected proxy. `send_sync` waits for the terminal HTTP callback before returning a body or error. This explains why a ping through JavaScript fetch does not exercise the same calling path. [AsyncHTTP, lines 459–597](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/http/AsyncHTTP.rs#L459). |
| Timeout | The client defaults to a 300-second idle/header timeout, with timer-wheel padding. HTTP-thread initialization reads the process variable BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_IDLE_TIMEOUT. This is a timing fact, not the demonstrated failure cause: the saved result is 503. [HTTP client, lines 266–303](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/http/lib.rs#L266), [HTTP-thread initialization, lines 1097–1109](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/http/HTTPThread.rs#L1097). |

The coordinator reports a user npm credential setting and no custom registry. I did not read credentials, `.npmrc`, global configuration or credential environment values. The source shows that such a configured credential can distinguish native audit from an anonymous probe. It does not prove that credentials caused this 503.

### Configuration isolation supported by 1.4.2

The pinned initialization reads an existing `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.npmrc`; otherwise it falls back to `$HOME/.npmrc`. It then loads the project's `.npmrc`. It does **not** consult NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG. A process-local XDG_CONFIG_HOME directory with an existing empty `.npmrc` therefore provides a source-supported way to isolate the user npm file without modifying it. Merely pointing at an empty directory does not suffice: the missing file triggers HOME fallback. Project configuration still applies. This mechanism is not tested by this investigation. [Pinned configuration loading, lines 1798–1839](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/install/PackageManager.rs#L1798).

A nonempty BUN_CONFIG_TOKEN, NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN or lowercase npm_config_token can subsequently supply a token. Setting these to empty strings does not clear an already-loaded token. A same-origin registry override can also retain credentials. Any coordinator-controlled isolation probe must account for these inputs without printing their values. [Pinned options, lines 602–639](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/install/PackageManager/PackageManagerOptions.rs#L602).

The [pinned npmrc documentation](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/docs/pm/npmrc.mdx#L5) agrees on XDG/HOME, project, bunfig, environment and CLI precedence. The [current unversioned documentation](https://bun.com/docs/pm/npmrc#which-files-are-read) additionally documents NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG. Its 1.4.3 page banner does not prove that every current-page feature exists in either pinned 1.4.2 or released 1.4.3. [Upstream PR 38047](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/38047) identifies the missing userconfig support directly. No version change is proposed.

## Confirmed local defect and remaining investigation

In `scripts/dependency-audit.ts:92–101`, the wrapper accepts exit code 1 as a possible vulnerability result, then calls JSON.parse before checking whether stdout contains a report. Empty stdout throws first, so the captured native stderr never reaches its intended error. This is a confirmed diagnostic defect. A correction should retain status, stderr and malformed/empty output as failure evidence; it must not turn a failed native audit into a clean result. No wrapper edit was made here.

At the first source-review checkpoint, the native 503 remained open. These were bounded hypotheses and distinguishing evidence, not selected causes. The later original-configuration control below rules out attributing the difference to credentials from these runs alone:

| Rank | Hypothesis | Evidence that distinguishes it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Authentication changes the server path or its failure behavior. | Compare the same pinned native request with only user-config credential isolation changed. Preserve project inputs and record token-variable presence without values. |
| 2 | The full package payload or its gzip representation triggers a backend failure absent from the small plain-JSON probe. | Compare equivalent gzip payloads and headers through another already-authorized client, then compare payload size/content separately. A successful single-package uncompressed POST cannot settle this. |
| 3 | Native synchronous transport framing or response handling differs from the successful fetch/curl requests. | Compare the same body, encoding, authentication state and endpoint while changing only client path. A TCP connection alone does not identify the failing HTTP phase. |
| 4 | A transient registry/backend fault affects the audit request. | Preserve the response status and timing for identical controlled requests. One later success would not explain the earlier failure by itself. |

The scoped primary-source search found the userconfig compatibility change. It did not establish a known upstream issue or released fix for this exact 1.4.2 request returning 503. Current-source or unrelated proxy issue claims are not evidence for this process. The coordinator owns any further experiment and native retry.

### Subsequent controlled results

The coordinator's credential-isolated native request returns 674 bytes of valid JSON with two advisories in 137 ms and exits 1. A second control removes only the user authentication setting, preserves the non-auth allow-scripts setting and project configuration, and runs the unchanged check runner's audit stage. It passes classification and all proofs in 212 ms. Global files remain unchanged.

The coordinator then repeats the original default configuration without an XDG override. Native audit succeeds in 106 ms with the **same** 674-byte JSON, SHA-256 `56ef184df747c8917737da61c7d4b055e5f466b4a2821194331c9209f42bc251`. The normal audit stage also exits 0; its saved output is `.artifacts/task12-audit-recheck.log`.

The sequence is two 503 responses followed by success under the same original configuration. These controls do not establish an account, credential, proxy or client defect as the native failure's cause. No global configuration change follows from them. They leave the separate wrapper error-masking defect reproducible and worth correcting without weakening audit acceptance.

This worker ran no audit, build, install, dependency update or process-control command. No root/global file changed. No waiver, timeout increase, security bypass or version change is recommended. A failed audit remains a failed gate. The only authored output is this report.

# Audit error diagnostic correction

Status: prepared for independent review and coordinator application. Repository source remains frozen at `5f74c3a0ceb57e2c5a54afe7e23bac91b9bbebb2`.

The proposed patch changes only JSON parse failure handling in the audit wrapper. It preserves the native exit status and stderr in the error, and keeps the parse error as its cause. Empty or malformed output remains a failed audit, including when the child exits zero. No public helper or dependency-injection interface is added.

Patch: [task12-audit-error-fix.patch](task12-audit-error-fix.patch). SHA-256: `29355318130d2526e6564e730904a113ac50194225221b4069fb759b1e24d017`.

The added test calls the actual exported auditDependencies function in a separate Bun process. It copies the source module and its two imports into a temporary repository.
